If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% in mid-horizon (days 15–25) to avoid overconfidence bias.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) over last 5 days, increase forecast by 2–5% in early horizon (days 1–10) to compensate for pessimism.  
When sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative (Δ > 0.5 in 3 consecutive days), reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in late horizon (days 25–30) to prevent momentum overcorrection.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 1–3% upward bias in mid-horizon to capture sentiment-driven momentum.  
If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, add 1–3% downward bias in early horizon to reflect sentiment-induced caution.  
If sentiment is mixed (alternating 0.33–0.67) and forecast deviates >3% from true path, apply linear correction: subtract 0.5% per 3 days of mixed sentiment in late horizon.
